summary: Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel is an Indologist who studied under Paul Thieme. He held posts at the Royal Library of Berlin (attested 1982, 1992–1994) and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1989, 2008).

Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Gakushuin University and the University of Tokyo (~1961–1967). He served as a professor at Nagasaki University (attested 1988) and founded the Japan Association for Bioethics in 1988.
Haruka Yanagisawa (1944–2015) was a historian and Indologist who held a post at the University of Tokyo (~1995–2007) and was affiliated with Chiba University (attested 2005).

Harumi Hirano Ziegler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her MA (-1994) and PhD (-2001) at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Harunaga Isaacson is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Groningen and Leiden University. He held posts at Oxford (1995–2000), the University of Pennsylvania (2002–2006), and the University of Hamburg (2000–2002; Professor from 2006).

Harushige Kōzu (1908–1973) was a linguist who studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo and at Oxford. He held teaching posts at the University of Tokyo from 1938 and became a professor and humanities dean at Musashi University in 1968.

Harvey B. Aronson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his doctorate under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1988) and co-directed the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism (attested 2001).

Harvey Paul Alper (1945–1987) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (~1968–1976) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Southern Methodist University from 1974 to 1987.

Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia (1908–1989) was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied under Henry Heras and later under F. J. Richards at University College London (~1934–1936), subsequently serving as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (1945–1946).

Haya Akegarasu (1877–1954) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and attended Otani University. He founded Seishinkai (1901) and served as head of administration at Higashi Hongan-ji (~1951–1954).

Heather Stoddard is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1967–1970) and was supervised by Nicole Vandier-Nicolas (~1977–1983), also studying with D. C. Lau and Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.

Heeraman Tiwari is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed his D.Phil. at Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He has held positions at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~2000) and Heidelberg University (2011–2012).
Hege Myrlund Larsen is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Bergen under the supervision of Bruce Kapferer (attested 2009).
Hegoda Khemananda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who served as Vice Principal of Vidyodaya Pirivena and Director of Dharma Paryeshanalaya (both attested 1993).

Heidi Fjeld is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her doctorate under Signe Howell at the University of Oslo (~2001–2006) and also studied at Oxford. She later served as a postdoctoral fellow at Oslo (~2007–2010).

Heidi I. Koppl is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the University of Copenhagen under Christian K. Wedemeyer and also studied under the traditional teacher Sherab Zangpo.

Heidi R. M. Pauwels is an Indologist who studied at KU Leuven and the University of Washington (PhD 1994 under Alan Entwistle). She lectured at SOAS (1994–1996) before joining the University of Washington faculty in 1996, becoming professor in 2002.

Heike Oberlin is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen and earned her PhD from the University of Würzburg. She has held teaching posts at Tübingen since 2005, serving as Associate Professor and Managing Director of Indology around 2014.

Heimo Rau (1912–1993) was an Indologist and art historian who earned his PhD at the University of Vienna. He worked at the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, directed Goethe-Instituts between 1960 and 1975, and taught at Heidelberg University (1968–1982).

Hein Htet Kyaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Edinburgh Napier University, James Cook University, and Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University. In 2024, he served as Director of Australasia for Atheist Alliance International.
